note: Growth METHOD base for mobile apps/games — generic, app-agnostic. MAINTENANCE RULE: once a method becomes a dated recommendation in advisor.json, or is implemented, DELETE it here (advisor.json becomes the single source); 'low impact + low effort' items are list padding and are never added. No generic ASO-101 content lives here. impact/effort: low|medium|high

items.title: Store page localization
items.desc: Even if the app itself stays English, translating the store listing opens a separate keyword index in every language. iOS bonus: some secondary locales (en-GB, es-MX) are also indexed in the main market → free extra keyword space.
steps: First wave: 6-10 languages chosen by audience, not by GDP
Do keyword research per language (never a literal translation)
iOS extra-locale trick: put different keyword sets in en-GB and es-MX
Translate screenshot headings for at least the top 3 languages

items.title: Ratings & review management
items.desc: Rating count and average are both a ranking signal and a conversion factor. Negative reviews that get an answer are frequently re-rated upward.
steps: Tie the native review prompt to an emotional peak (a record, a completed level)
Never ask on app launch
Answer every review within 48 hours
Reply to negatives with a fix + 'updated — would you try it again?'

items.title: Visual A/B tests (icon, screenshots)
items.desc: Changing the icon alone can move conversion by 10-30%. Without traffic a test never reaches significance — visibility first.
steps: Play: Store Listing Experiments, one variable, min 7 days
iOS: Product Page Optimization (up to 3 variants)
Icon first, then the first 2 screenshots
Ship the winner at 90%+ confidence, then start the next test

items.title: Apple In-App Events
items.desc: Event cards get their own listings in App Store search and on Today — visible to users who have AND have not installed the app. A free second storefront.
steps: App Store Connect > In-App Events
Tie it to something real in the app (a weekly tournament, a new theme)
Event card art + 30s video
Keep at least one event live per month

items.title: Google Play LiveOps / Promotional Content
items.desc: Play's event cards; they surface on the store home and on your listing. Apps that use them consistently report a visible lift.
steps: Check your Play Console access to Promotional content
Plan event/offer/major-update cards
Turn every major update into a card

items.title: Custom Product Pages (iOS)
items.desc: Up to 35 alternative store pages for the same app — land each ad campaign on the page matching its message. A serious conversion lever.
steps: ASC > Custom Product Pages
A screenshot set per campaign theme
Point Search Ads and social ad links at the CPP

items.title: Featuring nomination (Apple & Google)
items.desc: Editorial featuring is not a lottery — there is a form. 'Finished, polished, uses a new platform feature' plus a story raises your odds. If there is a story behind the app (solo development, reviving a classic, an unusual technical solution), that story is the real strength of the submission.
steps: Apple: the Featuring nomination form (ASC > Promote) — 3+ weeks before launch
Boil the story down to one sentence — the editor writes the shelf copy from it
Google: featuring is mostly automatic — good Android vitals and using new Play features are the signals

items.title: Play Shorts & the video-first store (2026)
items.desc: In 2026 Play opened a TikTok-like Shorts discovery surface. Vertical short video now feeds discovery inside the store itself.
steps: Reuse the vertical videos you make for TikTok/Shorts in Play's video slots
The first-3-seconds rule applies here too
Track the video/promotional surfaces in Play Console

items.title: Pre-registration — new app / major update
items.desc: A Play pre-registration page gives automatic install and a notification on launch day, amplifying the launch-week velocity signal.
steps: Open pre-registration ahead of a major update or sequel
Define a pre-registration reward
Attach a content calendar to launch day

items.title: TikTok/Shorts/Reels pipeline (3+ per week)
items.desc: Short video is the main discovery channel in 2026: roughly 59% of TikTok's gaming users say they discover new games there. One viral clip can be thousands of installs.
steps: Pick a format: satisfying moment / fail / dev-log
Capture raw footage at 60fps, cut to 15-25s
First 2 seconds: strongest moment plus a text hook
Reply to comments using the app's name (algorithm signal)
Post the same cut to all three platforms

items.title: Dev-log / the solo-developer narrative
items.desc: People subscribe to a story more readily than to a product. 'I built this alone in a year' is the highest-converting content indies have.
steps: 'After a year alone, my app is finally done' video
Before/after comparisons (old build vs new)
Share the failures too — a zero-downloads story is viral material

items.title: Reddit strategy
items.desc: One honest post in the right subreddit beats any ad. Anything that smells like advertising gets banned; story plus question works.
steps: Start with the obvious ones: r/AndroidGaming, r/iosgaming, r/IndieDev
Add topic communities: subreddits about what the app is actually for
Rule: 10 genuine participations per 1 promotion
AMA format: 'I built this alone, ask me anything'

items.title: Discord community + community-led growth
items.desc: A live Discord/Reddit community has become a primary acquisition source. For anything with a leaderboard, a tournament server is a natural fit.
steps: Open a Discord: a sharing channel + a weekly tournament channel
Put the Discord link inside the app
Tournament prize: a cosmetic or a name on the leaderboard
Give the 10 most active members beta access (ownership)

items.title: Press kit + niche press
items.desc: Big outlets are hard, but niche mobile sites and YouTube channels are hungry for content. A ready press kit makes saying yes ten times easier.
steps: A presskit()-style page: logo, icon, 5 images, video, description, developer story
Build a list of outlets that cover your exact niche
Email: 3 sentences + one image + a promo code
When a relevant news wave breaks, send again with that angle

items.title: Facebook groups (the 30-45 audience is there)
items.desc: The age segment TikTok does not reach (30-45) is still in Facebook groups. Groups about your app's subject — hobby, profession, nostalgia, local community — give organic reach without ads.
steps: Search for active groups about your app's subject (local + global)
Join as a member first; take part in the conversation
Post an image + link in a 'has anyone been looking for this? I built it' format
Mind group rules: some ban links — post the image and put the link in a comment

items.title: Web landing page + playable demo
items.desc: Google SEO brings traffic that has nothing to do with store search. A web demo → try → store link funnel works well for indies (if you can export a WebGL/HTML5 build).
steps: One-page site: video + demo + store badges
Blog: an 'apps like <closest competitor>' SEO article (you rank first in your own list)
QR code on any printed or video material

items.title: AI-assisted ad creative pipeline
items.desc: The 2026 standard is not a few polished videos but high-volume variation with AI. The rule: the product footage stays real, AI produces hooks/b-roll/variations (fake product footage risks platform penalties).
steps: Generate an AI video brief from Creative Studio
Produce 3-5s hook shots with Veo/Runway/Pika/Kling
Combine with real capture in CapCut
Test 3-5 variants a week, scale the CTR winner

items.title: UGC-style ads
items.desc: Real-user-reaction format is the highest-converting ad type of 2026 — it outperforms polished studio ads.
steps: Format: handheld camera + 'I tried this app' narration
Use AI-UGC avatar tools for zero-cost variations
Subtitles are mandatory (80%+ watch muted)

items.title: Store preview video
items.desc: On iOS it autoplays in search results — one of the single biggest conversion levers. Without one you are behind every competitor that has one.
steps: 15-30s, vertical, best moment in the first 3 seconds
No text, pure product + music
iOS: App Preview (screen-capture rules apply), Play: a YouTube link

items.title: Playable ad
items.desc: Brings the highest-intent users (they tried it, liked it, installed). Used on Unity Ads/ironSource/AppLovin/Meta.
steps: Produce a single-file HTML5 playable and upload it to the networks
Playable within the first 5 seconds, CTA at the end
A/B different difficulty and CTA moments

items.title: Apple Search Ads — keyword-precise start
items.desc: In-store search ads = the highest intent there is. It starts on a tiny budget and, as a bonus, shows which keyword actually converts — that intelligence feeds organic ASO.
steps: Exact match on your 2-3 highest-intent terms, $5-10/day
Start with Search Match off (protects the budget)
Move converting keywords into organic metadata
Match themes with Custom Product Pages

items.title: Google App Campaigns (UAC)
items.desc: Automated campaigns for Play installs. Little control, but the velocity effect on Play ranking can turn into organic lift. Don't burn money before conversion is proven.
steps: Fix store conversion first (otherwise the money is wasted)
Learn your CPI at $10-20/day
Creative: your best short videos

items.title: Micro-influencer swarm
items.desc: The 2026 model: 50-100 micro creators (10-50k followers, 2-5% engagement) instead of one mega. Scales on barter or low fees, and trust converts.
steps: TikTok Creator Marketplace or a hand-built list of creators in your category
Offer: early access + something exclusive + a small fee
Brief: 'play/use it your way' — never dictate a script
Track with a code or link

items.title: Soft-launch protocol: buy data with $200-500
items.desc: PROVE the product retains before scaling. The goal is data, not profit: run a small campaign in a low-CPI, culturally close market, measure D1/D7, then decide. Spending big before passing the D1 gate is burning money.
steps: Prerequisite: funnel events must be live in analytics
Google UAC: one market, $10-20/day, 14-21 days, 200-500 installs
D1 <20% → stop the ads, find the churn point, fix the product, retest
D1 20-30% → 2-3 improvements + a second $200 test
D1 >30% and D7 >10% → the scaling gate is open: raise budget gradually
Measure ARPDAU every round: no scaling without LTV > CPI

items.title: Treat D1/D7 retention as a growth tool
items.desc: Both stores weigh retention in ranking: the app that keeps users gets pushed. Casual game targets: D1 35%+, D7 12%+ (thresholds differ for utility apps — compare against your own category).
steps: Set up cohort tracking in your analytics
First session: reach the 'wow' moment within 60 seconds
Daily tasks + a streak system
A curiosity loop (wanting to see what is next) is the retention engine

items.title: Notification strategy (not spam)
items.desc: The right notification measurably lifts D7; the wrong one gets the app deleted.
steps: Social competition: 'your record was beaten'
Weekly event start
Ask for permission after the first success moment — never on launch

items.title: Android vitals & technical health
items.desc: Crash rate and ANR affect Play ranking DIRECTLY, and bad vitals disqualify you from featuring. Download size affects conversion too.
steps: Play Console > Android vitals: target 99%+ crash-free
Shrink the APK/AAB and the iOS binary
Test on low-end devices (most of Play's users are mid-range)

items.title: Catching a trend or news wave
items.desc: A news story, a viral trend or a competitor launch can spike search volume: a classic in your genre returning, a big rival shipping, a topic in your space hitting the news. Whoever is prepared wins.
steps: Google Alerts: your brand terms + your category terms + your closest rivals
Stock content ahead of the wave
On the day: promo text + an In-App Event + a content burst, all at once

items.title: Seasonal events & reskins
items.desc: A seasonal icon plus an event is a search and featuring opportunity on both stores. If the app already supports themes or visual variants, the cost is small.
steps: Plan 4 seasons a year: icon variant + theme + event card
Temporarily add the season keyword ('halloween', 'christmas')
Roll it back when the season ends (don't look stale)

items.title: Weekly radar scan routine
items.desc: You cannot grow what you do not measure. refresh.py plus your console data should be a weekly ritual.
steps: Schedule refresh.py weekly (Task Scheduler / cron)
Monday: read the Advisor tab and your console data
Send Claude the 'Interpret Radar Data' prompt

items.title: Console API integration (real impressions/installs)
items.desc: The App Store Connect API plus the Play Developer Reporting API pull impressions/installs/CVR automatically — the paid core of tools like App Radar.
steps: ASC: Users and Access > Keys > generate an API key
Play: a service account with Reporting API access
Give Claude the keys' location and have it wire them into refresh.py

items.title: Competitor intelligence routine
items.desc: A competitor's metadata change is a market signal. Track who moved to which keyword and who launched an event.
steps: Watch competitor metrics in the radar history
Add newly launched category rivals to the competitor list in config.json
Read competitors' release notes — what are they investing in?
